evidence.claim: Slack apps authenticate via OAuth 2.0 (v2 flow) to obtain access tokens
evidence.quote: Slack apps are installed with a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow.

evidence.claim: Web API requests are authenticated with bearer tokens in the Authorization header
evidence.quote: We prefer tokens to be sent in the `Authorization` HTTP header of your outbound requests.

evidence.claim: Anyone with a Slack account can self-serve register an app and obtain credentials
evidence.quote: You'll need to sign in to your Slack account to create an application.

notes: Multiple token types: bot (xoxb-), user (xoxp-), workflow (xwfp-), app-level, configuration, and service tokens; token rotation supported. Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp with its own OAuth user-token flow (oauth/v2_user/authorize). Free developer sandbox available via Slack Developer Program. Apps must be installed per-workspace; some workspaces require admin approval to install apps. GovSlack uses a separate OAuth domain.
